hook: Tapirs and anteaters living near development carry more microplastics in blood, and remote ones have some
hook_turn: carry more microplastics in blood, and remote ones have some
summary: Microplastic levels measured in free-ranging lowland tapirs and giant anteaters in Brazil rose with human footprint exposure and nearness to waste infrastructure, using GPS tracking. Animals in seemingly pristine areas also had microplastics. Two species and observational data, so causes are not isolated.
title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife.
